Villagers Of Village Karwari Kalan vs State Of Rajasthan on 19 January, 2023

For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Vijay Singh Yadav.
 Mr. Sunil Kumar Yadav.

For Respondent(s) : Ms. Sheetal Mirdha, Aag assisted by
 Mr. Prateek Singh.
Mr. Gaurav Singh.
Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Inderjeet Singh Order 19/01/2023

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioners with the following prayer:-
"It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that your lordship may graciously be pleased to admit and allow this writ petition and :-
(a) by an appropriate writ order or direction in nature thereof the respondents per directed to rehabilitate to the affected families of the villagers of village Karwari Kalan, Karwari Khurd, Rampuriya and Hathiyadeh in the vacant Charagah land of village panchauyat Karwari Kalan instead of Charagah land of village Panchayat Suwans.

(b) By an appropriate writ order or direction in nature thereof the respondents may be directed to constitute the committee under the provisions of section 45 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013;
(c) By an appropriate writ order or direction in nature thereof the proceedings of rehabilitation regarding the Hathiyadeh Medium Irrigation Project, whereby respondents initiate the proceedings for rehabilitation the affected families of the petitioners at Charagah Land of village panchayat Suwans, Tehsil Kishanganj,
District Baran may kindly be quashed and set aside.
(d) Any other appropriate writ order of direction, which this Hon'ble Court may deemed fit and proper, may kindly be passed in favour of the humble petitioners."
Counsel for the petitioners submits that the respondents are displacing the petitioners on account of construction of 'Dam' over (3 of 4) [CW-7667/2021] their lands.
Counsel further submits that the respondents are trying to rehabilitate them 50 kms away from their villages despite the land being available at nearby areas of their villages.

Counsel further submits that the respondents have not constituted the Committee under Section 45 of the Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter to be referred as 'Act of 2013') and prayed for allowing the writ petition and for giving direction to the respondents to allot them land at nearby areas of their villages.

sentences.text: Counsels appearing on behalf of the respondents opposed the writ petition and submitted that the respondents have duly constituted a Committee under Section 45 of the Act of 2013 vide order dated 18.02.2021 to rehabilitate the affected villagers.

They further submit that this Dam project is in the interest of public at large and the respondents will rehabilitate the affected persons at a suitable nearby place for which they have already identified the land which is only at a distance of less than 10 kms.
Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

This writ petition filed by the petitioners deserves to be dismissed for the reasons; firstly, the petitioners have no right for allotment of land at a particular place of their choice and it is for the State Authorities to rehabilitate the affected persons; secondly, the respondents have already constituted a Committee as provided under Section 45 of the Act of 2013 and the process for allotment of land to the affected persons is already going on and lastly, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, in my view, no case is made out for interference by this court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
] In that view of the matter, this writ petition stand dismissed.

(INDERJEET SINGH),J MG/359 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
